title: Price per item you actually use
hook: A ten-pack can have a lower sticker price per piece and a higher cost per used piece.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish purchase unit price from cost per utilized unit.

misconception: Lower cost per purchased piece guarantees lower cost per used piece.
objective: Distinguish purchase unit price from cost per utilized unit.

claims.text: Singles cost €0.50 each. A ten-pack costs €4. Unused pieces receive zero value in this model. Scaled model; unused pieces valued zero; fictional prices.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Used=5, A=0.5€/used and B=0.8€/used. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=0.5; B=["/",4,["min","x",10]]; x denotes Used. At x=5, A=0.5, B=0.8. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Here the relevant denominator is pieces used, not pieces purchased. Paying €4 and using five gives €0.80 per used piece. The model changes if the remaining pieces have value later.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=0.5; B=["/",4,["min","x",10]]; x denotes Used. At x=5, A=0.5, B=0.8. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Singles cost €0.50 each; a ten-pack costs €4 and unused pieces count for nothing. How many pieces must you use before the ten-pack's cost per used piece falls to €0.50? Correct: 8. Divide by pieces used, not bought: €4 ÷ 8 = €0.50; with fewer used, each used piece costs more.
